title: Board Book Toolbar — Usability Evaluation Report (Version 1 vs Version 2)
feature: Board book viewer toolbar (Version 1 Borderless dropdown · Version 2 Tool rail + labelled Download)
method: Synthetic Persona Usability Study | NN/G Methodology | 4 Personas | 11 User Stories | 2 Variants
disclaimer: All results come from simulated think-aloud sessions with synthetic personas. Numbers are simulated, not measured user data, and must be validated with real users.
context: Prototype at localhost:5173/board-book-page-nav.html?tab=v1 and ?tab=v2 with the real Q4 board pack (5 agenda items, 6 documents, 7 pages). Version 1 is the earlier all-tools-in-one-bar version with a borderless, hug-content document dropdown (max 200px, ellipsis). Version 2 is Version 1 with Search · Ask AI · Comment / Draw / Highlight moved into a floating vertical tool rail at the top-right of the document and a labelled 'Download' button in the top bar (Figma 32957:307272; it answers the UX feedback that the Search → Download → Ask AI order feels off). Both share the borderless dropdown, so this study isolates the rail and the labelled Download; the effect of the borderless dropdown itself (the earlier bar vs V1) is not isolated. Same personas and rules as the Version 1–3 study of 2026-10-23, with one new story (US11, download) because it was the subject of the feedback. Desktop (1280) and laptop / iPad landscape (1024) were screenshotted; below 1024 the viewer sits behind the Agenda / Board book segment and phones (<640px) keep the Document tools sheet, so those sizes were rated from the shared behaviour, not re-checked. Product decision 2026-10-23 (agenda open by default) is not built into either prototype; it does not differ between the two versions.

variants.name: V1 Borderless dropdown
variants.summary: Single top bar: contents toggle · borderless document dropdown (hug content, max 200px, ellipsis) · |< ‹ N / 7 › >| · zoom − % + · fit width · fullscreen · Comment · Draw · Highlight · Search · Download · Ask AI (all icon-only, tooltips on hover). Phone (<640px): the the earlier version Document tools sheet.

variants.name: V2 Tool rail
variants.summary: Top bar: contents toggle · borderless dropdown · |< ‹ N / 7 › >| · zoom − % + · fit width · fullscreen · a labelled 'Download' button. Floating vertical rail at the top-right of the document: Search · Ask AI, then (16px gap) Comment · Draw · Highlight, with tooltips opening to the left. Phone (<640px): unchanged the earlier version sheet.

goals.text: Assess discoverability: can each persona find Search, Ask AI, the annotation tools and Download without help.
Compare the load of one crowded top bar (V1) with two control zones (V2: bar + rail).
Evaluate control placement: distance from the reading point to the annotation tools, on desktop and iPad.
Check whether a text label on Download (V2) changes success for low-proficiency and touch users.
Quantify simulated task success and SEQ per user story, persona and variant.

stories.text: As a reader, I want to see which document and page I am on, so I don't lose my place.
As a reader, I want to read a document page by page without hunting for controls.
As a reader, I want to continue to the next document when I reach the end of the current one.
As a reader, I want to jump straight to the documents of a specific agenda item.
As a reader, I want to go to a page number someone mentions in the meeting.
As a reader, I want to zoom or fit a dense table so I can read the figures.
As a reader, I want to highlight or comment on a passage to discuss it later.
As a reader, I want to search the board book for a term.
As a reader, I want to read comfortably on a tablet or phone.
As a reader, I want to go back to the previous document.
As a reader, I want to download the board book so I can keep or annotate it offline.

personas.name: Margaret Chen
personas.goal: Check the final board pack end to end before it goes to directors.
personas.mentalModel: Keyboard shortcuts, dense toolbars, Notion/Acrobat-like patterns.
personas.risk: Impatient with extra steps; skims past labels.

personas.name: David Okafor
personas.goal: Review the pack and annotate items that need the Chair's attention.
personas.mentalModel: Explicit toolbar buttons and labelled Next / Previous.
personas.risk: Hesitates when something changes without explanation.
personas.emotion: Cautious; fears missing a document in a legal pack.

personas.name: Patricia Reyes
personas.goal: Open the pack and read the documents for one agenda item.
personas.mentalModel: A visible, labelled button for every action; step by step.
personas.risk: Ignores icon-only controls; never opens ⋯ menus.

personas.name: Robert Hale
personas.goal: Read the pack on iPad the evening before the meeting and mark questions.
personas.mentalModel: Reading app: swipe or tap to turn pages, everything within thumb reach.
personas.risk: No keyboard; low patience for admin-style UI.
personas.emotion: Time-poor; wants the right document fast.

MC.scenario: Opens the pack to spot-check the cover.
MC.behaviour: Reads the document name and N / 7 at once in both.
MC.friction: The borderless dropdown reads as a title; only the chevron and the hover fill say it is a menu.

MC.scenario: Gets to the end of the minutes document.
MC.behaviour: Presses → on the keyboard; no friction in either version.
MC.friction: |< >| are icon-only; their tooltips name the document but need hover.

MC.scenario: Goes to the page the Chair mentions.
MC.behaviour: Types the number in the page field.

MC.scenario: Zooms in on a dense table.
MC.behaviour: V1: finds − 100% + at once, hovers the fit-width and fullscreen icons next to it to read their names. V2: same controls, more air around them.
MC.friction: V1: zoom shares the bar with 12 other icons.

MC.scenario: Highlights a passage to raise in the meeting.
MC.behaviour: V1: scans the right end of the bar and finds highlight as the 3rd of 6 icons. V2: spots the rail beside the page and goes straight to it.
MC.friction: V1: tools sit far from the text she is reading.

MC.behaviour: V1: knows the tray icon and finds it between Search and Ask AI. V2: reads the labelled button at the far right.
MC.friction: V1: icon-only; the position between two other icons is the only cue.

DO.behaviour: Reads the name and N / 7 in both.
DO.friction: The name is no longer in a field, so he is unsure if it is clickable.

DO.scenario: Moves on to the next document.
DO.behaviour: Finds >| after a pause in both; hovers to read the document name.
DO.friction: The end of a document is silent; nothing says another one follows.

DO.scenario: Comments on a figure for the Chair.
DO.behaviour: V1: hovers three of the six right-end icons before finding the comment bubble. V2: looks at the top bar first, then notices the rail.
DO.friction: V1: icon-only row. V2: tools live in two zones (bar + rail).

DO.behaviour: V1: hovers Search, Download and Ask AI to tell them apart. V2: Search is the first icon in the rail.
DO.friction: V1: three similar icons side by side.

DO.scenario: Goes back to the previous document.
Downloads the pack for the file.
DO.behaviour: V1: recognises the tray icon after hovering. V2: clicks "Download".

PR.scenario: Opens the pack and reads the first page.
PR.behaviour: Reads the file name and 1 / 7 without interacting.
PR.friction: Page counter is global (N / 7), not per document.

PR.scenario: Gets to the end of the minutes document.
PR.behaviour: Notices >| after a long pause and tries it in both.
PR.friction: The end is silent; |< >| are icon-only.

PR.scenario: Looks for the documents of agenda item 3.
PR.behaviour: Does not click the borderless document name (reads as a title) and never opens the contents panel; asks for help.
PR.friction: Borderless dropdown has no field outline; the contents toggle is an unlabeled icon.

PR.behaviour: V1: ignores the row of icons at the right end of the bar and gives up. V2: sees a separate white card beside the page and tries its icons one by one.
PR.friction: Icon-only in both; in V2 the card at least separates annotation tools from the bar.

PR.scenario: Searches the pack for a name.
PR.behaviour: V1: does not find Search among six identical icons. V2: tries the first icon in the rail and finds Search; the sparkle (Ask AI) next to it confuses her.
PR.friction: Icon-only; Ask AI sparkle has no label.

PR.behaviour: V1: ignores the tray icon and looks for the word "Download". V2: clicks the labelled button.

DIR.scenario: Opens the pack on iPad (landscape) in the evening.
DIR.behaviour: Reads name and N / 7 in both.
Taps >| after looking for a swipe; both work after a pause.
DIR.friction: No swipe between documents; 32px targets at the top, far from a resting thumb.

DIR.scenario: Marks a question on a figure.
DIR.behaviour: V1: stretches to the top-right corner of the bar and mis-taps the neighbouring icon once. V2: the rail on the right edge is under the right thumb.
DIR.friction: V1: 32px icons packed in a row. V2: rail icons also 32px.

DIR.behaviour: V1: taps Search after trial and error. V2: Search is the top icon of the rail.
DIR.friction: Tooltips do not show on touch.

DIR.scenario: Reads on a phone on the train.
DIR.behaviour: Same Document tools sheet in both (existing behaviour, below 640px); not a differentiator.
V1: guesses the tray icon, no tooltip on touch. V2: taps "Download".
DIR.friction: V1: no label and no hover on touch.

shared: The end of a document is still silent in both: |< >| are icon-only and name the document only in a tooltip, so Patricia and Robert pause or stall at US03.
The borderless document dropdown has no field outline; it reads as a title for Patricia (US04) and leaves David unsure that it is clickable. Both versions share it.
Most controls are still icon-only in both (V1: all 15 buttons, V2: 14 of 15); tooltips need hover, which does not exist on iPad.

divergent.MC: Recognises the tray icon (V1); reads the label (V2)
divergent.DO: V1: hovers to confirm; V2: clicks the label
divergent.PR: V1: ignores the icon; V2: clicks the word
divergent.DIR: V1: no tooltip on touch; V2: taps the label

divergent.MC: V2 rail is faster than scanning the bar
divergent.DO: V1: hovers three icons; V2: finds the rail after the bar
divergent.PR: V1: gives up; V2: tries the rail's icons one by one
divergent.DIR: V2 rail sits under the right thumb

divergent.DO: V2: Search is the first icon in the rail
divergent.PR: V1: not found; V2: finds Search, unsure about the sparkle
divergent.DIR: Tooltips do not show on touch

divergent.MC: Fine — knows it is a menu
divergent.DIR: Uses the name only to read

heuristics.name: Visibility of system status
heuristics.evidence: The document end is silent; global N / 7 is read as document length (US03) — carried over from the Version 1–3 study.

heuristics.name: Match with the real world
heuristics.evidence: The sparkle (Ask AI) has no label; the borderless dropdown reads as a title (US04, US08).

heuristics.name: User control and freedom
heuristics.evidence: Previous page on the first page returns to the previous document; Esc leaves focus mode; the rail tools toggle off.

heuristics.name: Consistency and standards
heuristics.evidence: Same icons for the same actions in both; V2 uses one pattern (rail) for tools and one labelled button for Download.

heuristics.name: Recognition rather than recall
heuristics.evidence: V1: 15 icon-only buttons in one bar (US07, US08, US11). V2 labels one of them and groups the rest, a partial fix.

heuristics.name: Flexibility and efficiency
heuristics.evidence: Keyboard ← → crosses documents; the page field accepts direct input (US03, US05).

heuristics.name: Aesthetic and minimalist design
heuristics.evidence: V1 is crowded at the right end of the bar; V2 relieves the bar but adds a second zone.

heuristics.name: Help users recover from errors
heuristics.evidence: When Patricia believes the pack ended or a tool is missing, nothing helps her recover (US03, US07).

issues.issue: Document end is silent and the way on is an icon-only |< >| button whose name needs hover (carried over from the earlier study)
issues.impact: Patricia and Robert pause or stall at the document boundary

issues.issue: V1 puts 15 icon-only buttons in one top bar; Search, Download and Ask AI sit side by side with no label
issues.impact: Patricia cannot find Search, annotate or download; David hovers every icon

issues.issue: Borderless document dropdown reads as a static title (both)
issues.impact: Patricia does not open it to reach an agenda item's documents (US04)

issues.issue: V2 rail is still icon-only; the Ask AI sparkle and Draw / Highlight icons carry no label
issues.impact: Patricia only partly succeeds on US07 / US08

issues.issue: V2 splits tools across two zones (top bar + right rail)
issues.impact: David first looks for Comment in the top bar

issues.issue: Tooltips are the only names for rail and bar icons; touch has no hover
Contents toggle is an unlabeled icon and closed by default in either prototype (product decision 2026-10-23 says open)
issues.impact: Agenda items are reachable only through the dropdown

recommendations.title: Keep the labelled Download and extend labels to the rail on wide screens
recommendations.fix: Adopt V2's text button for Download. At ≥1280px let the rail expand to icon + text (Search, Ask AI, Comment, Draw, Highlight) or show persistent labels on touch.
recommendations.target: PR task success 67% → 83%+; PR US07 / US08 SEQ 3 → 5

recommendations.title: Use V2 as the base
recommendations.fix: Tools move next to the reading point and the top bar keeps navigation and zoom only.

recommendations.title: Give the borderless dropdown an affordance and test the earlier bar vs V1
recommendations.fix: Show a hairline border on hover / focus (or keep it visible below 1280px) and run a separate the earlier bar vs V1 comparison, because this study cannot isolate it.

recommendations.title: Make the document boundary visible
recommendations.fix: On the last page the next control reads 'Next document: <name>'; show local position ('Page 1 of 2 · 4 / 7') (carried over from the earlier study R1 / R3).

recommendations.title: Check the rail against the sheet at zoom above Fit and on tablet
recommendations.fix: It sits in the gutter at 100% on 1280 and 1024; verify it does not cover the sheet at higher zoom or under the open agenda, and keep it out of the way while panning.
recommendations.target: No overlap at any zoom; rail stays reachable

recommendations.title: Enlarge touch targets for the rail
recommendations.fix: Use 40–44px hit areas for the rail on touch devices; hold the 2px tertiary gap visually.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Validation
phases.text: Re-run V2 with R1 (labelled rail) against V2 as is, with the same persona types.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Isolate the dropdown
phases.text: Run the earlier bar vs V1 (same bar, bordered vs borderless dropdown) on US04 / US01 with Patricia- and David-type users.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Real users
phases.text: 2 real users per persona type incl. 2 directors on iPad landscape; tablet portrait and phone with the Agenda / Board book segment.

questions: Do readers expect annotation tools near the document (rail) or with the other controls (bar)?
Is one labelled button (Download) enough, or do readers also expect text on Search and Ask AI?
Does a borderless dropdown lower the discovery of the document list for occasional users?
Does the rail ever cover content on a dense table at higher zoom?
Which share of directors annotates on iPad vs desktop?

takeaways: Version 2 leads: the rail puts annotation next to the page and a labelled Download answers the original feedback — the biggest gains are for Patricia and Robert.
The gain comes from placement and one label, not from fewer controls: V2 still has 14 icon-only buttons, so labels remain the main fix.
The borderless dropdown is shared and unproven — test it on its own against the earlier version.
The document boundary is still the critical moment in both versions.
Validate with real directors on iPad before committing — the study is simulated and V2's rail was not checked above 100% zoom.

strengths.label: STRENGTH
strengths.text: Version 2's labelled Download is found by every persona (US11 SEQ 6–7); in Version 1 Patricia fails it and Robert and David only get partial success.

strengths.label: STRENGTH
strengths.text: Version 2's rail puts Comment / Draw / Highlight beside the page — highlight is faster for Margaret, and it is the only variant where Patricia gets any partial success on annotating (US07).
